# Pip-level pins, for readers who cannot use conda (env/README.md).
#
# ⚠️ 2026-10-03 — these used to be lower bounds (`numpy>=1.24.0`, `pandas>=1.5.0`,
# …), which directly contradicted `env/README.md` rule 1: "`numpy>=1.26` is not a
# pin. `numpy==1.26.4` is." They also disagreed with `environment.yml` and with
# the versions `code/analyses/reproduction_20261002/README.md` records as the ones
# the reproduction ran under. All three now name the same versions; every pin below
# was verified to resolve to a cp313 wheel before being written here.
#
# Python: 3.13.12   (env/environment.yml)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
numpy==2.4.4
pandas==3.0.3
scipy==1.17.1
statsmodels==0.14.6
matplotlib==3.10.8
seaborn==0.13.2
scikit-learn==1.7.2
pyarrow==22.0.0

# Reading the submitted documents and the published rasters. Both were unpinned
# until 2026-10-04 although 21 shipped scripts import them: every script under
# `code/figures/` reads either the Supporting Information .docx or a PNG through
# PIL, and `code/figures/ge_main/reproduce.sh` aborts in its preflight when PIL
# is absent — so the four main figures did not rebuild from a clean environment
# built from this file. Verified 2026-10-04: with both added, all four PNGs are
# byte-identical to the submitted figures.
python-docx==1.2.0
pillow==12.3.0

# Step 4 of code/run_all.sh reads the rendered PDFs' page geometry and font tables
# (`code/figures/11_figure_precheck.py` imports `fitz`). Added 2026-10-07 — it was declared
# in neither this file nor environment.yml, so step 4 raised ModuleNotFoundError in the
# shipped image; run_all.sh then reported it as "precheck reported non-blocking findings",
# which reads as a completed check with advisories. Measured: the precheck had never run
# inside the image. Version = the one the producing machine has.
pymupdf==1.27.2.3

# Note: S-PrediXcan is run separately via the command line (official MetaXcan
#       v0.8.1, installed from source — see env/Dockerfile).
# Note: Mahalanobis matching uses the R `MatchIt` package (env/renv.lock).
